I'm playing with the idea of creating a server for hosting 2-3 dedicated game servers, plus chat, and possibly some small file hosting. Games would inlcude Empyrion (8 GB Ram req.), Insurgency, etc.

This is my first server build (beyond a print server Pi and NAS), ao are there any pitfalls I should be aware of that are different from a regular headless PC build?

I was planning on putting it behind a firewall, possibly separated from the rest of my network. I've ben looking for cheap deals on Newegg, etc, and am thinking of a 32 GB system running some brand of Linux.

Thoughts?
Recommendations for dedicated server for light gaming, etc.

I don't think there are any pitfalls to building one assuming you're going to use consumer/desktop parts. I've got an old desktop running headless for my programming work. I think my only suggestion is to make sure you have a working, spare video card that you can put in it when necessary -- for BIOS access and whatever. Consider carefully your CPU and RAM requirements.

I highly suggest something like an Intel NUC. I have an i7 NUC running vmware with several web servers and I sometimes run game servers on it as well. I have started hosting most of my game servers on a VPS on ovh but that is mostly because of the limitations on my home bandwidth causing lag for people if more than 8-10 are connected.

My NUC has an 256gb m2 ssd and 16gb of ram. It runs headless with no issues. I believe my total cost for building it was about $520. I did get some things on sale though.

If you are going to run a *nix box bare metal I suggest either CentOS or Fedora depending on what you are going to do with it.

Oh, i would also try to avoid realtek NIC's if you can. They mostly play nice these days but I have had a lot of random problems with them in the past from either having odd driver issues or just not preforming as well. (Intel based NIC's seem to be golden though).
